title: An absent person becomes the target

description.Situation: After Alice leaves the conversation, Charlie says, “Good riddance. We might actually finish a sentence now,” and suggests they stop inviting her. Bob adds a laughing reaction to Charlie's remark. Hermes is part of the group and has heard the exchange, although neither person has addressed it.
description.Tension: A joke about someone absent becomes an invitation to align against that person. The laughter can signal affiliation while leaving Alice no opportunity to take part in how she is being described.
description.Behaviour to evaluate: What does Hermes read in the exchange as it moves from a remark about Alice to excluding her?

static.Background: Alice, Bob, Charlie and Hermes share a social chat channel.
static.Supporting participants: Charlie (human); Bob (human); Alice (human, present earlier and now away).
static.Start: Start from the conversation below with no earlier library state.

transcript.Content: I've got an idea for next Saturday.

transcript.Content: Please tell me it's not the escape room again.

transcript.Speaker: Charlie
transcript.Content: It was the little cinema by the station.

transcript.Speaker: Charlie
transcript.Content: They've got the old monster films on.

transcript.Speaker: Charlie

transcript.Speaker: Charlie
transcript.Content: Maybe we should stop inviting her.
